function: Learned bandwidth allocation for user-to-UAV A2G uplinks, jointly with slice-level and computing allocation and UAV trajectory, with self-adjusting slice reconfiguration minimizing system cost (p. 5, p. 7).
system: One UAV server (20-100 m) and 20 ground users on OFDMA A2G uplinks with 5/15 dB antenna gains; no RIS; 4 MHz, 0.1 m wavelength (p. 5, p. 11).
method: Self-adjusting two-timescale PPO (SaTPPO), on-policy actor-critic deep reinforcement learning with fully connected policy and critic networks; critic value gain triggers slice reconfiguration (p. 8, p. 9, p. 11).
data_channel: Custom simulator: distance-based A2G channel gain with antenna gains and path-loss index 2.2 [27]; 1 km smart campus with synthetic dynamic heterogeneous tasks (p. 5, p. 11).
test_conditions: 2500 training episodes of 200 slots, 1 km campus, 20 users; test episode in the same scenario; cost versus UAV computing capacity and bandwidth (p. 11, p. 12, p. 13).
baselines: Learned only: two-timescale PPO with fixed slicing windows (TPPO, several window sizes), and single-timescale PPO, SAC, and TD3; no non-learned baseline (p. 11, p. 13).
metrics: Cumulative reward (negative system cost), average task processing success rate, number of slice reconfigurations, slice resource ratios over time, and system cost (p. 11, p. 12, p. 13).
q1_support: p. 5: "The channel between the UAV and the smart terminals is a ground-to-air (A2G) channel." Its gain is a distance-based path-loss formula in a custom simulator; no 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO, or measured channel.
q2_support: p. 12: "during an episode of the testing phase of the proposed scheme" (same campus scenario). The sweeps over UAV computing capacity and bandwidth (p. 13) do not state that a trained model is reused in unseen settings.
q3_support: p. 11: "we choose three state-of-the-art reinforcement learning algorithms as the baseline schemes, namely PPO, soft actor critic (SAC), and twin delayed deep deterministic policy gradient (TD3)", besides TPPO; no non-learned method is compared.
q4_support: p. 11: "a fully connected layer with two hidden layers for both the long-timescale and short-timescale policy network structure"; no complexity order, operation or parameter count, or runtime is reported, only a convergence analysis (p. 10).
q5_support: p. 11: "we consider a smart campus scenario oriented to a square area with a side length of 1 km"; synthetic simulated data, with no code or data link and no public dataset.
notes: Include, area 6, by the aerial-link rule. Network slicing, computing allocation, and UAV trajectory are above the physical layer, but the short-timescale policy also outputs each user's bandwidth share on the OFDMA user-to-UAV A2G uplinks (p. 7: "which includes the allocation variables of computational and bandwidth resources for each user, and UAV trajectory planning"), which sets the uplink rate (Eq. (3), p. 5). Learned resource allocation in aerial links counts as physical layer, and learning it jointly with decisions above the physical layer passes the above_phy check; area 6 is the only area that fits. If the reviewer treats these bandwidth shares as slicing or edge-computing resources rather than physical-layer allocation, the decision becomes exclude, above_phy, p. 4 ("we divide the UAV-enabled physical network resources (including computational resources and bandwidth resources, etc.) into three independent virtual network slices"). The simulation section calls the method SaHPPO (p. 11), apparently a typo for SaTPPO.
